answer: Each agent holds a quill that signs one bid per time slice: work arrives as short auctions where every identity commits a verifiable block of compute time to compete. A mirror rule ties each bid to measured capacity, so an identity with no real machine behind it cannot win. One operator cannot run fifty identities at once because every bid burns actual compute and time; slices are non-transferable and expire within minutes. Over a long horizon, deliverers keep priority, while duplicate bidders bleed compute for nothing, so mass sybil creation costs more than honest participation.
